difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.8 at source lines 140-143: if A is an n-type and every B(a) is an n-type then Sigma x:A B(x) is an n-type. The proof (source lines 145-162) handles the two ends of the hierarchy separately and neither is a one-liner: the base case at lines 148-151 builds the centre of contraction of the sigma type componentwise, while the induction step at lines 153-161 first has to replace the path space of the sigma type by the equivalent type Sigma p : a_1 = a_2, trans p b_1 = b_2 using the sigma path theorem (line 158), then invoke preservation of n-types under equivalence (line 159) before the inductive hypothesis applies. The statement gives no hint that the transport of b_1 along p is what has to be shown truncated.
